svg.title: Proof. Start with [lN, uN] in (FCA2) and descend. If an interval carries trajectories through levels i+1, . . . , N with endpoint level-(i+1) couplings li+1, ui+1, apply (FCA3) to the level-(i+1) curve; the crossings (FCA6) and Lemma 14.23 give a closed subinterval on which the level-i coupling stays in [li, ui] and attains both endpoints. Retain the higher states and insert the new coarse state; every higher density identity, startup condition and continuity estimate survives restriction. At level zero l0 = 3 ̄β/4, u0 = 5 ̄β/4, and the intermediate value theorem gives b∗. For (FCA8) induct upward: solving (FCA3) for the fine coupling and using (FCA4), the increment lies between 3 4s log Li and 5 4s log Li, while bβi+1 −bβi = s log Li.
